content.comment_body: Hello, does anyone know if there is an interrupt function available in [product_name] that can interrupt an ON DELAY timer? After a power outage, I need the function to resume with the remaining accumulated time. Thank you for any advice.
Hi, [product_name] does not have interrupt capabilities. However, you can enable retentivity for timers and counters to preserve their state in case of a power failure. Regards, [user_name]
I suggest using a counter with retentive memory. For instance, you could count 1-second pulses from a pulse generator. Hope this helps!
Why do you recommend using a counter? Does using a counter provide more functionality than simply enabling the retentivity feature on the ON DELAY timer block?
Using the retentive ON DELAY is a good solution. Alternatively, using a counter also preserves elapsed time, even if the input signal turns off, and you can add a reset button for separate control.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for an interrupt function for ON DELAY timers in [product_name], especially to retain and continue the timer's accumulated value after power outages. Responses clarify that interrupts aren't supported, but retentivity is available for timers and counters. The discussion includes alternative approaches and opinions on best methods for maintaining timer states across power cycles.
